items.section: I. Algebraic groups, torsion, and the norm argument
items.title: An additive automorphism to test the chosen linear structure
items.analysis: Over \(\mathbf F_p\), the map \(a:\mathbf G_a^2\to\mathbf G_a^2\), \((x,y)\mapsto(x+y^p,y)\), is an additive group automorphism with inverse \((x,y)\mapsto(x-y^p,y)\), because \((y+z)^p=y^p+z^p\). As a morphism of group schemes it cannot be represented by a constant \(2\times2\) matrix: its first coordinate contains the degree-\(p\) monomial \(y^p\), which has no expression as a degree-one polynomial in \(\mathbf F_p[x,y]\). Which linear structure does the manuscript choose so that its particular descent cocycle avoids this obstruction to a direct GL(n) argument?
items.context_comparison: This sharpens the descent-method link to MPL_131 RN001 and the question on scan 044, while the context supplies no such choice of linear structure.
items.confidence: high for the explicit group-scheme automorphism; unresolved for the manuscript’s implicit choice
items.reason: Polynomial inverse and additivity identities; comparison of coordinate-polynomial degrees

items.title: The C2 regular norm tests the excluded case
items.quote: “on vérifie facilement que ce deuxième cas est exclu”
items.analysis: Take \(k=\mathbf C\) and \(\Gamma=C_2=\{1,s\}\), the constant one-dimensional \(\mathbf F_2\)-module for the trivial absolute Galois group, so its nonzero module is irreducible. In \(A=\mathbf C[C_2]\), multiplication by \(s\) in the basis \((1,s)\) has matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), determinant \(-1\), and hence \(\Gamma\cap\ker N=\{1\}\). Does this concrete instance expose an omitted treatment of the \(\ell=2\), one-dimensional case in the sentence excluding it?

items.section: J. The final Tsen and coefficient-comparison leaf
items.title: A nonzero cocycle killed by the coefficient inclusion
items.analysis: For \(K=\mathbf C(t)\), all roots of unity \(U\) lie in \(K\), and \(c(g)=g(\sqrt t)/\sqrt t\in\mu_2\subset U\) is a continuous nontrivial character of \(G_K\), because the \(t\)-adic valuation shows \(t\) is not a square in \(K\). Every \(U\)-valued coboundary is \(g(u)/u=1\), so \([c]\ne0\) in ordinary \(H^1(K,U)\), but under \(U\hookrightarrow(K^{\mathrm{sep}})^*\) the same cocycle is the coboundary of \(\sqrt t\). Does this exact calculation explain why the corrected degree range \(i>1\) must be retained, and what additional convention is needed before applying it to the hatted notation?
items.context_comparison: No supplied context entry settles this map; the same coefficient inclusion also tests the unqualified degree-one passage on scan 048, giving a direct connection within the current package.
items.confidence: high for ordinary continuous H1 with discrete coefficients; unresolved for the source’s hatted convention
